messages.subject: Ordinal data via latent specification
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to translate a model from JAGS into Stan. That is a simple model with on ordinal variable (Y, with three categories) and 2 covariates (X1 and X2). JAGS codes is as followed:

model{
for(i in 1 : Nobs) {

Z[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], 1) # Latent variable
Y[i] ~ dinterval(Z[i], cut[1:4]) # Observed, ordinal variable

mu[i] <- beta[1]*X1[i]+beta[2]*X2[i]

}
for(j in 1: 2){
delta0[j] ~ dnorm(0, 1.0E-6)
}
delta[1:2] <- sort(delta0[1:2])

cut=c(-1.0E10, delta[1], delta[2], 1.0E10)

for (i in 1:2){
beta[i]  ~ dnorm(0.0, 1.0E-6)
}
}

However, I have not found any functions in Stan that is equivalent to dinterval in JAGS, which connects the observed and latent variables.

Do you have any ideas?

Thank you so much!
Tran.

messages.author: fa6f5d4c13c0cca5
messages.subject: Re: Ordinal data via latent specification
parts: I would recommend looking at the section in the Stan manual on Ordered Logistic and Probit Regression (6.7); it talks about ways to deal with ordered response variables.

messages.subject: Re: Ordinal data via latent specification
parts:
Thank you, I did it successfully for the case of one ordinal variable.

My question is in the case where we have more than one ordinal. In that case, I would like to use latent (normal) variables because using them helps me easily to specify the correlation.

In other words, I am working with multivariate linear regression where the outcomes are ordinal.

Best,
Tran.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Ordinal data via latent specification
parts:
Did you ever figure this one out? (I'm trying to clean out
old unanswered user email).

The short answer is that you can do the same thing with
the marginals of a multivariate regression --- use cutpoints
as in an ordinal logit to map a univariate scalar to an ordinal.

- Bob
